findings.title: build_24cal_12dev=false is a miscount in the reviewer test, not an author bug
findings.reasoning: rev2_full.py L136 requires len(bc)==24 CAL builds AND len(bd)==12 DEV builds (36 total). v4_runner.run loops 2 prefixes x 6 sites = 12 configs and calls build_pack exactly twice per config: once CAL at the config prefix (L200) and once DEV at 512 (L201). Hence the correct counts are 12 CAL + 12 DEV = 24 total, matching the instrumented rec_counts.build_calls=24 (bc=12, bd=12). Expecting 24 CAL builds would mean two CAL builds per config, which the runner does not do and which fit_config_12_contexts=true (12 distinct fit contexts) contradicts. The DEV side is pinned by dev_always_512=true and 72 DEV score calls at 512 rows (144 total = 12 configs x 6 models x 2 cohorts => 12 DEV packs). Correct expectation: 12 CAL (one per config) + 12 DEV.

findings.title: cal_prefixes_correct=false is the same miscount

Actual CAL builds: 6 sites at prefix 256 + 6 sites at prefix 512 = 12 entries ([256]*6+[512]*6), one CAL build per config. Anti-leakage is independently confirmed WITHOUT this check: no_dev_leaks=true and leaks=[] (instrumented check_sources raises on any DEV source in any fit; all 120 fit calls used exactly the 11 CAL sources, all_fitters_CAL_only=true), cal_scored_prefix_rows=true (CAL scored at its config prefix row count), dev_scored_512_only=true (every DEV score at 512 rows), prefix_fits_distinct_P_Q_alpha=true (finalizer re-verified from raw VB_LOCAL_FITS.json: P_sha256, Q_sha256 and alpha_Q0 all differ between 256|site and 512|site at all six sites), and score-key coverage is exactly {256,512} x 11 sources per cohort.

findings.title: readout_ratios_sensible=false applied a ratio threshold to a relative risk
findings.reasoning: rev2_full.py L211-213 requires 1.0 < source_equal_relative[m] < 2.0 for the four readouts. source_equal_relative is the RELATIVE risk r=(M_m-M_Q1)/M_Q1 (v4_runner.aggregate L154-163), measured r in [0.0388, 0.0552] — correctly OUTSIDE (1,2). The intended quantity is the ratio M_m/M_Q1 = 1+r in [1.0388, 1.0552], which IS inside (1,2) for all 8 readout entries (finalizer check readout_r_values_and_ratio_sensible PASS). The probe's ratios_in_1_to_2=true independently confirms sensible ratios at high04/256 (1.1294-1.1790). The readouts are sensible; the check compared the wrong quantity. STABLE_FREE_LINEAR is deliberately excluded from that check's model list; its large r is a genuine overfitting finding (see OBS-1), not a scaling defect.
